methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.0x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Lab 91, a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Anand Chamarthy, has raised $10M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems, though the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or similarly-tiered datapoints for statistical reliability.

The stage-progression method is the only applicable triangulation approach. Using total raised ($10M) as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields $25M. This methodology is straightforward but relies on the assumption that funding amount correlates reasonably with valuation; it does not account for dilution, burn dynamics, or product-market progress since raise close.

Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied: while the median P/S across the three public semiconductors is 21.0x, Lab 91's revenue is not disclosed and remains unknowable for private companies. A peer-median approach likewise fails due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables—the broader 12-company semiconductor peer set lacks three or more companies at the same valuation tier and stage. Given these constraints, the analysis supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, centered at $25M. Key uncertainties include the timing and terms of the last $10M+ raise, current burn and runway, and whether recent technical or commercial milestones have shifted the risk profile since funding close.
